text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - Britain's leading stock index ended slightly lower after robust U.S. economic data knocked down the Dow industrials and offset the nearly nine percent jump in the shares of Lloyds TSB Group . The FTSE 100 closed at 4899.3, down 8.2 points, or 0.17 percent. This was up 47.8 on the week.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse dealings generally lower as Daimler-Benz AG took a beating after two major investment banks lowered earnings estimates on the industrial group. The DAX-30 index closed at 4408.79, down 30.14 points, or 0.68 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4336.98, down 68.54 points, or 1.56 percent up 91.15 from last week.

ZURICH - The Swiss bourse was closed today for the national day holiday. On Thursday the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) slid 31.3 points or 0.53 percent to 5,898.2 points. There was a rise of 51.2 points from the previous Friday. The Swiss market index closed at 5898.2, down 31.3 points, or 0.53 percent.

MILAN - Italian shares closed largely steady after a volatile trading session on Firday following stronger than expected U.S. July jobs data and the July NAPM survey which both hinted at inflationary pressure in the U.S. economy. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 14695, up 1 points, or 0.01 percent down 399 since last Friday.

PARIS - French shares ended in loss, pushed down by falls in the bond markets, following a stronger-than-expected U.S. NAPM reports which indicated upward price pressures, traders said. The CAC-40 index closed at 3049.44, down 26.23 points, or 0.85 percent a rise of 23.5 from a week ago.

AMSTERDAM - The Dutch AEX share index ended down 2.59 points at 980.74, mirroring the Dow's drop which was triggered by the release of the July NAPM index. The AEX index closed at 980.74, down 2.59 points, or 0.26 percent down 82.9 from last Friday.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks slumped to end more than two percent lower after a technical glitch which halted electronic-system trades on the Tokyo bourse throughout the morning brought on shower of arbitrage-linked sales when trading resumed after the lunch break, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19804.38, down 527.05 points, or 2.59 percent a fall of 585.16 on the week.

HONG KONG - Kong Hong stocks extended their record-breaking rally and the Hang Seng Index eked out a closing high, but trade was volatile with profit-taking on banks and utilities alternating with buying on property stocks. The Hang Seng index closed at 16379.22, up 13.51 points, or 0.08 percent a gain of 721.1 since last week.

SYDNEY - Depressed mining stocks and weakness on Wall Street on Thursday took its toll on the Australian share market. Stocks ended 0.3 percent lower although advances outnumbered declines. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2727.5, down 7.6 points, or 0.28 percent up 36.3 from a week ago.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial shares finished weaker but off day's lows, trickling down on Wall Street's overnight slide after its recent bullish run, dealers said. The All-share index closed at 7456.8, down 27.7 points, or 0.37 percent. This was up 12.8 since last Friday. The All Gold index closed at 963.7, down 18.1 points, or 1.84 percent a fall of 6.1 from last Friday, while the Industrial index closed at 9145.5, down 5.0 points, or 0.05 percent up 91.1 on the week.
